state.final_answer:
**Problem summary:** A 52-year-old man with chronic diarrhoea, breathlessness and fatigue has historical cardiac biomarker elevation, mild renal impairment, a resected sessile serrated lesion, negative monoclonal protein studies, and echocardiographic/CMR features strongly suggestive of infiltrative cardiomyopathy, most plausibly amyloidosis.

The symptom cluster—chronic diarrhoea with new breathlessness and fatigue—points towards a systemic process rather than an isolated gastrointestinal disorder. Historical values (NT-proBNP 887 pg/mL, hs-troponin 23.9 ng/L, creatinine 1.3 mg/dL, eGFR 62.7) indicate cardiac strain and mild renal impairment at that time; current status is unknown and must be re-assessed.

Echocardiography (symmetric LV thickening, LVEF 36%, grade-II diastolic dysfunction, relative apical sparing) and CMR (high native T1, markedly raised extracellular volume ~50%, diffuse subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement including interatrial septum) together support an infiltrative process, with cardiac amyloidosis the leading hypothesis. The resected serrated lesion explains neither the diarrhoea nor the cardiac findings; bile reflux gastritis is incidental. Negative serum/urine immunofixation and free light chains argue against AL amyloidosis from a detectable clone but do not exclude amyloidosis overall—wild-type transthyretin or hereditary forms remain possible, and occult monoclonal disease cannot be fully excluded.

What is not established: tissue diagnosis, amyloid subtype, and the cause of diarrhoea (which could reflect autonomic/gastrointestinal amyloid involvement or a separate process). Priorities before final aetiology: current vital signs and bloods, tissue confirmation via an appropriate biopsy site, typing of any deposited material, transthyretin sequencing if typing suggests it, and evaluation of the diarrhoea.
